title: promote-latest: escape log-derived diagnostics for C1, DEL and bidi, and comment that a non-empty others suppresses condition 2
description: Follow-ups from the round-2 Opus review of opum-ai/lore-cli#625 (landed as d434a273), relayed by team-lead 2026-10-20; filing only, not started. (1) MINOR: scripts/promote-latest.mjs condition-2 diagnostics (the lines that JSON.stringify annotations[0] and strangers[0]) print a log-derived ##[error] line to stderr. JSON.stringify escapes U+0000-U+001F but NOT C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F, including 8-bit CSI U+009B and OSC U+009D), DEL, or bidi overrides. Both print sites predate #625; what is new is that --allow-escape-sequences now lets ANSI-bearing log content reach them, where before gh refused and nothing arrived. Escape those classes, or stop quoting the line, with a test proving a C1/DEL/bidi payload is neutralised. (2) NIT: add a one-line comment at the `if (!others.length)` guard that a non-empty others suppresses condition 2, so a run failing condition 1/4 never reports its condition-2 state; it is why mutation predictions kept missing. (3) RECORD: gh must accept `gh api --allow-escape-sequences`; the real --dry-run against run 39366418979 from the PR branch and from dev (2026-10-20) already proved it does, which is the citation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: log-derived diagnostics are escaped for C1, DEL and bidi (or no longer quoted), proved both ways with a payload test and a mutant
a comment at the others guard states it suppresses condition 2
the gh --allow-escape-sequences requirement is recorded with the 39366418979 dry-run citation
